label: Engineering Manager
title: Engineering manager ladder
description: Explore the draft manager ladder across results, people, and vision and strategy. The source directs readers to a manager or HR for official guidance.

axes.label: Results
axes.description: Set goals, measure outcomes, and sustain accountability at increasing scope.

levels.summary: Set measurable goals for direct reports, align their work with team goals, and monitor feedback loops.
Set team goals, earn team buy-in, intervene when feedback shows a problem, and hold the team accountable.
Align goals and outcomes across multiple teams, improve feedback loops, and unblock delivery.
Coordinate goals and dependencies between teams, design feedback loops, and hold team leads accountable.
Align department goals with the business, prioritize critical outcomes, and hold managers accountable.

axes.label: People
axes.description: Hire, coach, develop, and support teams as managerial scope expands.

levels.summary: Run regular one-on-ones, execute a team hiring plan, and discuss each report's development.
Own the team interview process, understand career ambitions, and identify useful training.
Improve hiring and create growth opportunities, promotion coaching, and training across teams.
Improve hiring across teams and contribute to consistent career and training frameworks.
Plan organizational hiring, improve engineering-wide interviewing, and maintain career ladder standards.

axes.label: Vision and Strategy
axes.description: Communicate a destination, define how to reach it, and measure alignment.

levels.summary: Understand the company and team vision, communicate it to direct reports, and align team work.
Identify a team area that needs clearer vision or strategy and improve how progress is measured.
Define a vision and strategy for multiple teams with metrics that indicate progress.
Coordinate vision across teams and plan for cross-departmental effects and adoption.
Manage multiple strategies and establish a framework for tracking success and alignment across the department.
